morning_soundtrack.title: Pearl Jam Share Statement About New Drummer At Ohana, Eddie Vedder Performs With Pixies, Bad Religion, Billy Strings, Stephen Wilson Jr., & More
morning_soundtrack.snippet: Over the weekend, Eddie Vedder's Friday set at California's Ohana Fest turned into a Pearl Jam performance with Abe Laboriel Jr. behind the drum kit and they played with him again last night. They were the band's first gigs since Matt Cameron left after 27 years .
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: The bittersweet electricity of watching a beloved band navigate an uncertain new chapter in real time, live under the California sun.

morning_soundtrack.title: Smush Announce New Album i’ll always wish,,: Hear “milkweed butterfly”
morning_soundtrack.snippet: In February, Brooklyn-via-Vancouver group Smush made me understand Norah Jones and Owl City in a whole new way. Their covers EP Standards , which also featured takes on Big Rig, Hotline TNT, and Field Medic, breathed kinetic glitchy/shoegazey bliss into modern classics. Today, they're back with new original music: a spiky single, "milkweed butterfly," that announces their sophomore album i’ll always wish,, coming early next year.
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: Like catching a firefly in a jar — delicate and luminous, but buzzing with something restless underneath.

morning_soundtrack.title: Finally a Festival That Went Off Without a Hitch: Bourbon & Beyond 2026 Recap + Photo Gallery
morning_soundtrack.snippet: Acts like Foo Fighters, Queens of the Stone Age, Chris Stapleton, Mumford & Sons, Dave Matthews Bands, and Kacey Musgraves helped make the Louisville festival a wonderful, easy-going time. Finally a Festival That Went Off Without a Hitch: Bourbon & Beyond 2026 Recap + Photo Gallery Jonah Krueger
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: The relief of a deep exhale after a long week, cold bourbon in hand, watching the sunset over a crowd that just wants to have a good time.

morning_soundtrack.title: Michelle Branch Kicks Off Sold-Out “Everywhere and Back Again Tour” With Career-Spanning Set
morning_soundtrack.snippet: The show celebrated her 25 years in music with a set that leaned into her first two albums. Michelle Branch Kicks Off Sold-Out “Everywhere and Back Again Tour” With Career-Spanning Set Travis Bland
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: The warm ache of singing every word to a song you forgot you still knew by heart.

morning_soundtrack.title: John Mayer Announces 2027 Las Vegas Sphere Residency
morning_soundtrack.snippet: Each show will feature three different sets: solo, with a full band, and with the John Mayer Trio. John Mayer Announces 2027 Las Vegas Sphere Residency Eddie Fu
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: Polished, ambitious, and just a little too calculated — like a Vegas skyline at midnight, dazzling but never quite intimate.

morning_soundtrack.title: Luthier on Luthier: Chris Holcomb
morning_soundtrack.snippet: Chris Holcomb specializes in making world-class resonator guitars in Santa Cruz, California. Chris built a guitar in his teens and has pursued the craft ever since. In episode 118, Chris tells us this wasn’t a straightforward path, but one of persistence and dedication that ultimately paid off as he achieved his goal of making The post Luthier on Luthier: Chris Holcomb first appeared on Fretboard Journal .
morning_soundtrack.vibe_check: The quiet satisfaction of sawdust on a workshop floor and a craftsman who chose the long, unhurried road to mastery.

global_silver_linings.title: Good News in History September 29
global_silver_linings.snippet: 30 years ago today, the Nintendo 64 video game console was released in North America. Critically acclaimed as “quite simply, the fastest, most graceful game machine on the market”, the N64 was one of the first gaming consoles to have four controller ports and could handle a 4-player split-screen without significant slowdown. Named after its […]
global_silver_linings.reason: History is full of quiet turning points and unsung breakthroughs worth remembering — pausing to celebrate them reminds us that progress has always been possible, even in difficult times.

global_silver_linings.title: ‘The forest is life’: how Indigenous communities in Peru are preventing wildfires
global_silver_linings.snippet: Forest fires have ravaged Peru in recent years, but Indigenous communities are fighting back, protecting forests and reducing blazes
global_silver_linings.reason: Indigenous communities in Peru are drawing on generations of traditional knowledge to protect their forests from wildfires, proving that the people closest to the land are often its most effective guardians.

global_silver_linings.title: A Place to Sleep for Denver’s Homeless College Students
global_silver_linings.snippet: This story was originally published by Chalkbeat. Sign up for their newsletters at ckbe.at/newsletters. During her first semester at Chicago’s Malcolm X College, Nikya Harrell had had enough.
global_silver_linings.reason: A practical shelter solution for homeless college students in Denver shows that communities can find targeted, dignified ways to keep determined young people on their feet and in school.

global_silver_linings.title: What Japan’s 107,677 centenarians reveal about diet, lifestyle, and aging
global_silver_linings.snippet: BY THE OPTIMIST DAILY EDITORIAL TEAM There are 107,677 people in Japan who are currently aged 100 or older, according to recently released health ministry figures. That puts Japan ahead of every other country for centenarian population, and it is the first time the country has crossed the 100,000 mark. The survey tracking this figure […] The post What Japan’s 107,677 centenarians reveal about diet, lifestyle, and aging first appeared on The Optimist Daily: Making Solutions the News .
global_silver_linings.reason: Japan's remarkable population of centenarians offers real, evidence-backed clues about how everyday choices — what we eat, how we move, how we connect — can add years of healthy, meaningful life.

discovery_articles.title: Meet the 'Fire Amoeba,' a Newfound Blobby Organism That's Defying Expectations About How Much Heat Complex Life Can Handle
discovery_articles.snippet: The newly described species, found in Northern California's Lassen Volcanic National Park, can still reproduce at 145 degrees Fahrenheit and move around at 147 degrees, according to a new study
discovery_articles.ferns_note: A blobby single-celled creature thriving in near-boiling volcanic pools just quietly rewrote the rulebook on where complex life can survive. Everything we thought we knew about heat tolerance had, apparently, not yet met this particular amoeba.

discovery_articles.title: Who Wrote Elizabeth I's Most Scathing Letters? New Research Suggests the Tudor Queen's Male Secretaries Revised Her Correspondence to Emphasize Her Temper
discovery_articles.snippet: An analysis of more than 500 missives found that Elizabeth's advisers crafted and even intensified the expression of emotion in her messages to such figures as Mary, Queen of Scots, and James VI of Scotland
discovery_articles.ferns_note: The most feared pen in Tudor England may have belonged not to Elizabeth I, but to the men quietly sharpening her words behind closed doors. History remembered her fury; turns out, some of it was a committee effort.

featured_read.title: Hernan Diaz’s New Novel Isn’t a Dystopia—Trust Him
featured_read.snippet: Pulitzer winner Hernan Diaz releases his first novel in four years this week, and he’s parrying a few questions about genre. “I take issue with the word dystopia,” he replies to an opening inquiry. “I don’t think Ply is a
featured_read.blurb: Hernan Diaz resists the dystopia label for his new novel *Ply* with characteristic precision — and the distinction he's drawing turns out to matter enormously. A conversation about what fiction can do that genre can't.

reading_room.title: How Biden Averted a War With Iran
reading_room.snippet: In April 2024, the U.S. military helped avoid a wider conflict in the Middle East by working with Israel to defeat an Iranian missile attack.
reading_room.blurb: The spring 2024 Iranian missile barrage nearly rewrote the map of the Middle East, and this piece reconstructs the quiet, high-stakes hours in which it didn't. A rare look at diplomacy and deterrence working in real time.

reading_room.title: The Edge of California Is Falling Into the Ocean
reading_room.snippet: Storms driven by El Niño are pulling chunks of coast away.
reading_room.blurb: California's coastline isn't eroding — it's collapsing, in chunks, into the Pacific, and El Niño is only accelerating what was always coming. A grounded, unsettling account of land that has simply stopped holding on.

reading_room.title: Paternity is poetical
reading_room.snippet: The notion that fatherhood and creativity are at odds is plain wrong, as both poetry and neuroscience are showing us - by Daniel Swift Read on Aeon
reading_room.blurb: The old myth that fatherhood drains creative life turns out to be, on neuroscientific and poetic evidence alike, quietly backwards. Daniel Swift makes a case that parenthood doesn't interrupt the artistic mind — it reorganizes it.

reading_room.title: Frogs Wear Bacterial Armor to Defend Against Fungus
reading_room.snippet: It gives them a leg up in survival
reading_room.blurb: Some frogs have struck an evolutionary bargain with bacteria, wearing living microbial armor against a fungus that has driven dozens of amphibian species to extinction. A small, startling story about survival through symbiosis.

reading_room.title: The end of humanity
reading_room.snippet: Instead of accepting that humanity will soon be obsolete, we can build a better future with respect for human traditions - A film by Andreas Dürr and Jan-Marc Furer Watch on Psyche
reading_room.blurb: Rather than treating human obsolescence as a foregone conclusion, this essay-film asks what it would actually mean to build a future that still has room for human tradition, ritual, and meaning. A necessary counterweight to the acceleration narrative.

garden_note.note: There's a particular clarity to a Zürich morning at the end of September — the air carries that first real bite of alpine autumn, and the garden is doing that bittersweet thing of looking both spent and quietly magnificent at once. Step out before the mist lifts from the Limmat valley and you'll catch the asters still holding their violet crowns like they haven't heard the news.

news.title: The Brilliant Grocery List Trick This Award-Winning Financial Expert Swears By
news.snippet: The cost of groceries has been on the rise for years, and many of us are feeling the impact. The average American spends nearly 13% of their household budget on food (or roughly $10,169 per year), according to a report from CashNet USA. And within the past year, food prices jumped by 3.4 percent, according to the USDA.
news.blurb: A genuinely clever read for anyone who suspects their grocery habits are quietly bleeding the budget dry.

news.title: Sanjana Modha’s quick and easy recipe for baked beans butter masala | Quick and easy
news.snippet: Transform two tins of baked beans into this creamy curry Masala baked beans, tadka baked beans, curried baked beans, spicy baked beans; all avatars of spice-laced baked beans are a mainstay of British Asian kitchens. We were raised on this stuff – use as a toastie filler, to smother jacket potatoes, or scoop them up with roti. Enter baked beans butter masala.
news.blurb: A delightful little trend dispatch on how two humble tins of baked beans have quietly become a canvas for beautiful, spice-forward British-Indian home cooking.

news.title: A Chef’s Guide to the Best Restaurants in Asheville, North Carolina
news.snippet: Rachael McIntosh Meherwan Irani, of Chai Pani and Spicewalla, shares his go-to places to eat and drink in his adopted hometown.
news.blurb: Consider this your insider's pocket guide to one of America's most quietly exciting food cities, courtesy of someone who actually cooks there.

recipe.title: Perfectly Moist and Sweet Cornbread
recipe.snippet: Perfectly Moist and Sweet Cornbread Some cornbread is too dry. Some cornbread is too sweet. This cornbread is juuuuuust right!
recipe.blurb: This is the cornbread you'll want to pull from the oven on a cool evening — moist, gently sweet, and gloriously unfussy, the kind that makes a simple supper feel like a proper occasion.

larder.seasonal_note: Zürich's markets are brimming with Zwetschgen right now — those deep-indigo Italian prunes that make the most fleeting, buttery Zwetschgenwähe of the year; seek them out at Helvetiaplatz before the weekend crowd strips the stalls bare. A slow Tuesday morning with a warm slice and a milchkaffee is, frankly, a form of Alpine self-care.

fern_data.greeting: That particular early-autumn chill — the kind that bites the back of your hands but not yet your face — is a good companion for this morning's edition. Japan's 107,677 centenarians have thoughts on how to live in it longer, and Elizabeth I's secretaries have been caught sharpening her fury behind her back.
